newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says IMF talks might be in March or April.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says IMF talks might be in March or April.

text.p: The timing of Turkey's talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has not yet firmly been decided but they could be held in March or April, senior Turkish officials said on Tuesday.
"There is no firm date for talks now. The date is determined mutually by the two parties," a senior government official said.
"We can have them in March or even in April depending on the agendas of the sides," he said.
The IMF team's visit was originally planned for February but officials gave no reason for delay.

Turkish bankers have urged the government to reach a new stand-by accord with the IMF and draw up a medium-term stabilisation programme narrow big public deficits, estimated at over 10 percent of the country's gross national product.
